title: Krishna and the big snake.
lines: This is a story from India, about little Krishna.
Krishna was a little boy with blue skin.
He wore a peacock feather in his hair and he played his flute beautifully.
He lived in the village of Gokul, by the river Yamuna.
Krishna looked after the cows with his friends.
Every day they took the cows to the meadow by the river.
The grass was green there and the water was cool.
The boys played, and the cows ate grass.
But one day something strange happened.
The cows drank the water from the river.
And straight away they fell over.
A few boys who had drunk the water felt ill too.
The birds flying over the river fell into the water.
The flowers on the bank turned brown.
An old man from the village knew.
In the deep water of the river, he said, lives a big snake.
His poison makes all the water dirty.
I'm going to talk to Kaliya, he said.
He climbed a tall tree by the river.
A tree that was still green.
He looked at the dark water.
His friends ran to the village.
Krishna has jumped into the river!
And his daddy, and all the people of the village.
Deep under the water Kaliya woke up.
Who dares to swim in my river?
He came up, with his five big heads.
But Krishna grew bigger and bigger.
So big that the snake had to let go of him.
And then Krishna jumped onto the snake's heads.
He danced from one head to the other.
He danced gracefully and lightly, but every step was as heavy as a mountain.
He sank deeper and deeper into the water.
Kaliya, he said sternly, you have made the water dirty.
Go to the big sea, said Krishna.
There's plenty of room for you there.
Kaliya and his family swam away, far away, to the sea.
Krishna stepped out of the water.
The water became clear and blue.
And the cows stood up again.
Yashoda took Krishna in her arms.
She gave him a thousand kisses.
But never just jump into the river again!
That evening the whole village had a party.
And now when the people of Gokul look at the clear river, they think of little Krishna who danced on the snake.
